Carport addition · construction concept set

Casa 5400 Carport

A 17'-0" × 34'-0" flat-roof carport attached to the north wall of the house. It starts at the back corner of the house and runs 34' east over the driveway, jutting 10'-7" past the front toward the street. Steel frame, stucco fascia, recessed LED soffit and a teak slat wall along the hedge, sized to shelter the FJ40.

Sheet G-0

Site analysis

G-0

What the survey tells us

Lot
100.00' deep × 75.00' wide, 7,500 sf, street frontage on SW 116th Ave (east).
House
23.45' × 41.60' one-story, long side faces the street. FFE 10.71'; yard grades 9.3'–9.6'.
North yard
22.39' from the north wall to the north (bush/hedge) line. This is where the carport goes.
Front yard
32.90' from the house's NE corner to the front property line.
Driveway
Existing 12.7' × 30.5' concrete, plus the new square pavers along the north wall (photo 3).
Obstacles
4' chain-link fence and gate line at the house's NW corner; metal shed ~12'-9" west of the rear wall; overhead utility line crossing the back yard, well clear of the carport.

Layout decision

The carport starts at the back (west) corner of the house and runs 34' east along the north wall toward SW 116th Ave. That covers the full 23'-5" wall and juts 10'-7" past the front of the house over the driveway. The teak slat wall runs the full length of the north side, between the columns and the hedge. The back end lines up with the existing 4' chain-link fence and gate line, so that stays put.

Side setback conflict. At 17' wide the north edge sits 5'-4" from the property line. RU-1 zoning requires an interior side setback of 10% of lot width, which is 7'-6" on this 75' lot. You need either a variance / administrative adjustment, or a width of 14'-10" max.
Front setback. The carport front sits 22'-4" from the front property line. RU-1 allows 15' for up to 50% of the building width and 25' for the rest. So this works if the 17' carport counts inside that 50%, which the zoning reviewer confirms at plan review. If they say no, shorten the projection by 2'-8" to hold 25'.
Lot coverage. House 976 + shed 115 + carport 578 = 1,669 sf, or 22%. The limit is 40%.

Sheet S-2 · Section A–A looking west

Building section

S-2
  • Clear height 9'-0" under the soffit. An FJ40 with a roof rack is about 7'-0", so there's headroom for a rack and a tall van.
  • The roof drains away from the house at ¼" per foot (4¼" over 17'). It falls to a hidden gutter at B-1 with downspouts concealed in the C-1 and C-3 wraps, discharging to a dry well in the north strip. Miami-Dade requires stormwater to stay on your lot.
  • The house's north eave gets cut back to the wall. The new membrane turns up under the existing roof edge with counter-flashing, which is the #1 leak point, so it needs a roofer with a Miami-Dade NOA-listed system.
  • Verify the house has a continuous concrete tie beam at the top of the CMU wall before relying on the ledger. If it doesn't, add intermediate columns along the house side.

Controls

  • A downlights: smart dimmer (e.g. Lutron Caseta) at the house wall by the front, plus a 3-way companion inside the kitchen/front door. Schedule 30% dusk-to-11pm with full brightness on motion.
  • B uplights and C sconces: the transformer's photocell handles dusk-on, with an auto-off timer.
  • Keep all lighting on one 15A circuit. The total connected load is about 160W (1.3A), well under the 80% continuous limit of 1,440W.
Sheet E-2 · one-line & wiring schematic

Electrical schematic

E-2

Circuit schedule

CktBreakerWireServes
L-115A 1P#14 THWN-2 (use #12 for drop)10 downlights, transformer, sconces
R-120A 1P#12 THWN-22 GFCI receptacles
EV-150A 2P#6 THWN-2 CuOptional EV charger (NEC 625)

Wiring rules to follow

  • The soffit is a damp location, so no Romex (NM-B). Run THWN-2 in PVC or ENT through the joist bays, or use UF-B.
  • For the underground run from the house to C-2, use Sch. 40 PVC at 18" cover. Under the driveway, Sch. 80 or 24" cover.
  • Rough in all conduit before the pavers are reset, and add one spare ¾" conduit to C-1 for a future gate operator or camera.
  • Bond the steel frame to the equipment grounding conductor with #6 Cu.
  • Before adding EV-1, run a load calculation on the existing panel. Older 100A panels in Westwood Lakes often need an upgrade.
Sheet P-1 · general contractor sequence

Build sequence

P-1

  1. Confirm zoning and jurisdiction

    Look up your folio on the Miami-Dade Property Appraiser site to confirm unincorporated Miami-Dade, RU-1 zoning and your flood zone. Decide between 17' with a variance and 14'-10" by right.

    Week 0–1

  2. Hire design team

    Hire a Florida-licensed architect or engineer for sealed drawings: site plan on your survey, foundation, framing, connection details, wind-load calcs, electrical plan, and NOA numbers for roofing and any products.

    Weeks 1–4

  3. Zoning relief (if keeping 17')

    File an administrative adjustment or variance for the 2'-2" side setback reduction. Neighbor notice is typical; a support letter from the north neighbor helps a lot.

    +6–12 weeks

  4. Permit

    Submit a building permit with an electrical sub-permit to Miami-Dade RER. You can pull it as an owner-builder (you must live there and do or directly supervise the work) or have a licensed GC pull it.

    4–10 weeks review

  5. Site prep

    Call Sunshine 811 for locates. Lay out the column grid from the property pins, lift pavers at the footings and trench, relocate the chain-link gate, cut back the north eave, and root-prune the hedge line.

    2–3 days

  6. Underground electrical

    Trench and lay PVC from the house to C-2 and C-1, plus the spare conduit.

    Inspection · underground electric

  7. Footings

    Excavate five 4'-6" pads (expect limestone; rent a breaker). Place rebar, set anchor rods with a plywood template, get the inspection, then pour. Cure 7 days before steel.

    Inspection · footing

  8. Ledger and steel

    Epoxy-anchor the 3×12 ledger to the tie beam. Erect the galvanized columns and W10 beams (a small crane or boom truck for half a day), then grout the base plates.

    Inspection · framing/structural

  9. Roof framing and deck

    Install the 2×12 joists in hangers with H10A ties, sloped ¼"/ft north. Sheathe with 19/32" ply on the HVHZ nail pattern.

    Inspection · roof sheathing nailing

  10. Roofing

    Install the NOA-approved TPO or mod-bit system, flashing into the house roof, hidden gutter and downspouts.

    Inspection · roofing in-progress + final

  11. Electrical rough

    Set the wafer-light J-boxes, sconce boxes, receptacle boxes, switch and transformer locations, and pull the wire.

    Inspection · rough electric

  12. Soffit, fascia, stucco

    Install lath on the fascia and column wraps, then smooth stucco and a stucco or aluminum soffit. Paint with elastomeric to match the house.

    Inspection · lath

  13. Slat wall

    Install the ipe or thermally-modified slats on galvanized steel girts along the north side, between the columns, with ¾" gaps. Leave the gaps open; they let wind through and keep the hedge breathing.

    3–4 days

  14. Trim-out and site

    Install fixtures, GFCIs, the dimmer and the transformer, then aim the uplights. Build the dry well, reset the pavers, and replant.

    Inspection · final electric

  15. Final

    Final building, zoning and electrical inspections, then the certificate of completion. Send it to your insurer, because it can affect your wind premium.

    Inspection · final building

Once the permit is issued, construction takes about 8–12 weeks. Allow 4–7 months from design start to final, plus 2–3 months if you need a variance.

Sheet C-1 · Miami, 2026 dollars

Rough cost estimate

C-1
Budget alternative
$28k – $45k

Same footprint using a Miami-Dade NOA aluminum insulated-panel carport from a specialty installer. It comes with its own engineering and has recessed lights pre-cut in the panels. You give up the stucco fascia and the teak screen.

Owner-builder savings
−12% to −18%

Acting as your own GC and subbing out the steel, roofing, stucco and electrical removes most of the overhead & profit line. You take on scheduling, inspections and liability.

These are budget ranges for planning, not a bid. Get three quotes from licensed Miami-Dade contractors on the sealed drawings.
